newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SOCCER-GRASSHOPPER, AJAX FIGHT FOR PLACE IN LAST EIGHT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GRASSHOPPER, AJAX FIGHT FOR PLACE IN LAST EIGHT.

text.p: Grasshopper Zurich have Ajax Amsterdam on the ropes and can deliver the knockout punch to the four-time European Cup winners with a draw in their final Group A Champions' League clash on Wednesday.

The battered Dutch champions, European Cup finalists for the last two years, will limp into a cold, sold-out Hardturm Stadium needing a win to keep alive any serious hope of reaching the quarter-finals and salvaging something from what, thus far, has been a disappointing season.

The surprising Grasshoppers, who earlier stunned Ajax 1-0 in Amsterdam with midfielder Murat Yakin's ferocious long-distance free-kcik, need only a point to propel them into the final eight for the first time.
Level on nine points with Grasshopper and French champions Auxerre, Ajax could sneak through with a draw but only in the unlikely event that Auxerre lose at home to struggling Glasgow Rangers.
The Dutch will be buoyed by the fact they have not lost an away game in Europe in the last three seasons but will have little else to boost their spirits.
One of Europe's most decorated clubs, Ajax have offered few glimpses of such form in recent efforts.

On Saturday, the Amsterdam side drew 1-1 with lowly Groningen, leaving them sixth in the Dutch table and faced with the prospect of entering the mid-winter break out of Europe and out of league contention.
But going into Wednesday's crucial match, Ajax will be suffering from more than wounded pride.
Coach Louis van Gaal has kept team doctors busy, using 23 players in five Champions' League matches because of injury.
Nigerian winger Tijani Babangida returns from injury but Richard Witschge and Peter Hoekstra remain in the infirmary.

A desperate van Gaal is contemplating rushing the returns of international defenders Frank de Boer and captain Danny Blind for the crucial match and there is even a chance that Finn Jari Litmanen may come on as a late substitute if Ajax are chasing the game.
De Boer appears to be finally over an ankle injury and Blind has also been training after a long lay-off but still seems likely to miss out on the group A match in Zurich.
Grasshopper will enter the pivotal match without key striker Kubilay Turkyilmaz and defender Bernt Haas after both picked up second yellow cards in their 2-1 loss to Rangers two weeks ago.
The absence of the two Swiss internationals, however, will be tempered by the return of Yakin and Romanian striker Viorel Moldovan, the Swiss league's leading scorer with 17 goals.
Moldovan is expected to be joined up front by Swiss international Nestor Subiat, who is returning to his best form after being sidelined for almost a year with an Achilles tendon injury.

The Swiss club will be well rested, having not played for over a week after wintry conditions forced the postponement of their Saturday league match. The same bitterly cold conditions are forecast for Zurich on Wednesday.
That will not suit Ajax, who now play their winter home matches under the sliding roof of their Arena stadium.
